aramco_cm_schedule_safety.ai_message: The honest version: your two schedule-critical units are also your two highest-exposure units, so pressure on the schedule lands exactly where the risk already is. The turnaround is on day 11 of 24 and running about a day and a half behind on the Unit 2 hydrocracker. This morning's two expired hot-work permits are a symptom of that — the night shift kept working past a validity window rather than stopping to re-issue. Stopping that work costs hours against a critical path. Not stopping it costs a hot-work job running unauthorized in a high-hazard zone. The third option is the one TrackLynk makes available: re-issue in minutes with conditions held against a live gas test, so the work continues legitimately instead of continuing quietly.

aramco_cm_headcount.ai_message: Because three systems are measuring three different things and none of them is wrong. The gate counts badge-ins and cannot tell that a tag was left in a locker, so it over-reports — 2,440 today. The permit system only counts people working under an open permit, so it never sees support and logistics — 2,400. Contractor timesheets arrive on each company's own cadence and lag by hours — 2,380. TrackLynk resolves to 2,412 by matching badge-ins to live location, and holds the 28 it cannot match rather than counting or discarding them. That last part is what makes the figure defensible: the exceptions are visible, not absorbed. The reconciliation is logged, so the number you give the regulator has a document behind it.

aramco_cm_surge.user_query: What happens at the next surge?
aramco_cm_surge.ai_message: Contractor headcount goes toward 3,000 and daily permit volume roughly doubles. Verification capacity does not double, so the share of high-risk work that actually gets checked falls — and today, at 2,400 people, you are already producing three jobs outside their permit conditions in a single morning. The exposure does not scale linearly with headcount; it scales with the gap between permits issued and permits verified, and that gap widens fastest exactly when contractor density peaks. Standing the live permit-and-location view up before the surge, rather than during it, is the difference between adding verifiers and not needing to.
